name: mcdaniel-2019-treatment
title: Fluid challenge and antibiotic in severe sepsis (McDaniel et al. 2019, Figs 9-10)
question: In the severe infection, what do the paper's 1000 mL saline challenge at 44 h (Fig 9) and 4.5 g piperacillin/tazobactam at 46 h (Fig 10) do to volume, pressure and the pathogen?
hypothesis: The challenge raises blood volume and pressure above the untreated arm within the hour it is given; the antibiotic's plasma level exceeds the pathogen's MIC (16 mg/L) and the blood pathogen falls below the challenge-only arm's by 52 h.
objective: Starting from the severe infection's state saved at 44 h, run biogears_sepsis (60 s updates) to 52 h untreated, with treatment fluid_challenge (2 x 500 mL saline at 50 mL/min at 44 and 44.5 h) and with treatment antibiotic (the challenge, then 20 mL PiperacillinTazobactam over 30 min at 46 h).

literature_anchors.expectation: Fig 9: the 1000 mL saline challenge transiently raises SBP and urine output
Fig 10: piperacillin rises above the MIC (16 mg/L) during the 30 min infusion and the pathogen declines

runtime.note: Every arm starts from the severe infection's state saved at 44 h (viva_biogears/states/StandardMale@severe-infection-44h.xml), as McDaniel et al. started each treatment from a saved septic patient state; the protocol keeps engine time (hours since the infection), recorded as protocol.branch_h. An 8 h arm takes about 1.5 h of wall time. mcdaniel-2019-sepsis/run.py runs the same arms outside the workbench; analyze.py draws Figs 9-13.

units_and_time.scale: one recorded row per 60 s update; global_time counts from the saved state (engine time = protocol.branch_h + global_time)
units_and_time.note: BioGears' own clock; its internal solver step is 0.02 s.
Saline (BioGears' Saline compound) set by the protocol.

expected_behavior.name: protocol-is-delivered
expected_behavior.condition: both treated arms give 1000 mL of saline, all between 44 and 45 h; the untreated arm none

expected_behavior.name: challenge-restores-volume
expected_behavior.condition: at 45 h the challenge arm has more blood volume and a higher MAP than the untreated arm

expected_behavior.name: antibiotic-clears-pathogen
expected_behavior.condition: piperacillin plasma concentration exceeds 16 ug/mL; blood pathogen at 52 h is below the challenge-only arm's and below its own value at 46 h

controls.name: untreated
controls.hypothesis: The severe infection left untreated is the reference.
controls.expected: No saline, no drug; identical to the treated arms until 44 h.

controls.name: fluid-challenge
controls.hypothesis: For the antibiotic, the challenge-only arm differs only by the drug.
controls.expected: Identical to the antibiotic arm until 46 h.

robustness.note: BioGears is deterministic; the arms are identical until their first action, which tests/test_treatment.py checks.

predictions: Paper Fig 9: the challenge transiently raises SBP and urine output; Fig 10: piperacillin rises above the MIC within the 30 min infusion and the pathogen declines.
preregistered.thresholds_provenance: The MIC (16 mg/L) and doses are the paper's; every other criterion is a direction, not a fitted number.
preregistered.pilot: Not piloted: each arm is a 52 h run. The protocol mechanics were tested on the engine with short timings (tests/test_treatment.py, tests/test_protocols.py in the package).

falsifiability: Refuted if the challenge leaves blood volume or MAP at 45 h at or below the untreated arm's, if piperacillin never exceeds 16 ug/mL, or if the pathogen at 52 h is not below both the challenge-only arm's and its own value at 46 h.
limitations: The paper does not give the bolus rate or the bag used for the antibiotic; these follow BioGears' own InfectionSevere.xml (50 mL/min boluses; 20 mL PiperacillinTazobactam at 0.667 mL/min).
The untreated progression differs from the paper on 8.2.0 (no septic shock by 48 h; see mcdaniel-2019-sepsis), so the challenge is given to a less hypotensive patient than the paper's.
The saved 44 h state comes from the severe arm of mcdaniel-2019-sepsis (run.py, 60 s updates); BioGears is deterministic, so the arms continue that run exactly.
